scope_note: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net.

estimates.label: Reported 2022 real-property transaction anchor

period.label: Reported 2022 sale of the reused data-center property

scope.label: Real property at 4777 W Ironwood Drive, Franklin, Wisconsin

interval.interpretation: The point carries the reported transaction price into the modeled account without adding other project measures; it is not a statistical estimate.

parameters.name: reported_transaction_price

provenance.detail: Sale price attributed by the article to a Wisconsin state record

parameters.transformation: Retained without adding assessments, permits, taxes, or hiring plans

estimates.confidence_rationale: The published price is property specific and the buyer release independently matches the asset and lease, but the underlying state transfer record was not reproduced.
estimates.decision_relevance: Preserves the only public transaction-value anchor while preventing an adaptive-reuse ownership transfer from being mislabeled as new construction or operator capital expenditure.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Recorded deed instrument, Expedient tenant-improvement spending, IT-equipment investment, annual capital expenditure, financing, rent, and locally retained investment

assumptions: The published price and buyer release refer to the same 4777 W Ironwood property.
An asset ownership transfer is not treated as construction spending, assessed value, local output, or Expedient capital expenditure.

limitations: The price is from secondary reporting that cites a state record.
The buyer release confirms the asset and lease but does not disclose price.
The transaction may include lease and financing attributes not separately valued.
It does not measure new local economic activity.
estimates.notes: Standalone investment-context anchor only; never add it to assessments, permits, property tax, construction spending, or operating contribution.

estimates.label: Modeled construction-eligible share of the 2025 building permit

period.label: Permit PB25-0303 issued during 2025; completion and expenditure timing unverified

scope.label: Interior alteration and exterior mechanical-yard work at 4777 W Ironwood Drive

interval.interpretation: The PB25-0303 administrative permit value is multiplied by 60%, 80%, and 100% construction-eligible shares. This is a last-resort scope sensitivity, not observed spending, a true-value bound, or a confidence interval.

provenance.detail: Lower building-work share after excluding possible IT equipment and other nonconstruction capital
Central building-work share after excluding possible IT equipment and other nonconstruction capital
Upper scenario treating the full permit amount as construction eligible

estimates.confidence_rationale: The project-specific permit and scope are direct local records, but the city form identifies project cost as estimated and no equipment split, invoice, completion or payment was public.
estimates.decision_relevance: Provides the narrowest reproducible construction scope for decision testing without applying employment or local-purchase multipliers that the Franklin audit could not defend.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Invoices, actual construction outlays, IT-equipment costs, completion timing, contractor identity, payment records, worker hours and payroll

assumptions: Construction-eligible shares are 60%, 80%, and 100% solely for scope sensitivity.
PM25-0174 is not added because its mechanical scope may overlap PB25-0303.
Permit value is an administrative estimated-cost basis and is not relabeled as realized spending.

limitations: Permit value may differ from contracted or paid cost and is not a bound on actual spending.
Equipment content is parameterized rather than observed.
The 2022 and 2025 permits are not summed across unrelated periods.
No construction jobs, local purchasing or multiplier effects are inferred.
estimates.notes: Scope-control sensitivity only; excludes the real-estate sale, assessments, tax payments, hiring forecast, PB22-0043, and potentially overlapping PM25-0174.

estimates.label: Annual local public-service-cost break-even threshold

scope.label: Parcel 9301001000 property-tax account spanning the same local taxing jurisdictions

interval.interpretation: The threshold equals the verified recurring parcel-tax contribution by definition; it is not an estimate of actual public-service cost.

estimates.confidence_rationale: The threshold identity is exact for the verified tax principal, while actual same-scope marginal public cost is unavailable.
estimates.decision_relevance: States the public-cost level that would offset the verified recurring tax contribution without manufacturing a cost or net position.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Project-attributable fire, police, road, utility, administrative, infrastructure and financing costs for the same recipients and period

derivation.formula: annual marginal local public-service cost at break-even = verified parcel property-tax contribution
assumptions: The threshold is an identity, not an observed cost.
The 2025 zero special-assessment row does not imply zero public cost.
No state incentive, permit, assessment, ownership-transfer amount, interest or penalty is netted into the annual local account.

limitations: Actual public-service cost is unobserved.
No positive or negative fiscal margin is asserted.
The parcel payment spans several recipients whose marginal costs may differ.
estimates.notes: No net fiscal result and no actual public-service-cost estimate; this is only a same-scope break-even threshold.

estimates.label: Modeled annual facility electricity

period.label: Annualized engineering sensitivity using the current 1.6 MW critical-load capacity

scope.label: Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin at 4777 W Ironwood Drive

interval.interpretation: Low, central, and high pair 25%, 50%, and 75% critical-load utilization with PUE 1.2, 1.4, and 1.6. This is a last-resort engineering sensitivity, not a meter reading, true-value bound or confidence interval.

parameters.name: critical_it_capacity

provenance.detail: Current operator-reported critical IT load capacity

parameters.transformation: Converted to kW and multiplied by hours, utilization, and PUE

provenance.detail: Low PUE sensitivity informed by national engineering ranges
LBNL 2014 average PUE benchmark used as high sensitivity

estimates.confidence_rationale: Capacity is project specific, while exhaustive operator, PSC, utility and municipal searches found no MKE1 utilization, meter or site PUE; those parameters dominate the range.
estimates.decision_relevance: Converts the capacity stock into a reproducible annual electricity sensitivity after direct meter evidence was exhausted, without treating capacity as consumption.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Interval-metered electricity, utility bills, peak load, occupied IT load, site PUE, renewable procurement, rate impacts, water, wastewater and emissions

derivation.formula: critical IT capacity × 1,000 kW/MW × 8,760 hours × utilization × PUE
assumptions: Endpoint utilization rates are 25%, 50%, and 75%.
Endpoint PUE values are 1.2, 1.4, and 1.6.
Reported critical IT load is nameplate capacity, not observed demand.

limitations: No site meter or bill.
PUE and utilization are assumptions or transferred benchmarks.
The interval is not a bound on actual use.
No facility water, wastewater, emissions, renewable share or utility-system cost is inferred.
estimates.notes: Engineering sensitivity only; the 1.6 MW capacity remains the direct observation and the model is not added to any fiscal or output measure.

estimates.label: Modeled county real GDP comparison gap

period.label: 2024 Milwaukee County outcome relative to a mechanically matched benchmark; Expedient opening year 2021

scope.label: Expedient Franklin facility and Milwaukee County

interval.interpretation: The envelope is plus or minus twice the 2013-2020 pre-period RMSE. It is a fit sensitivity, not a statistical confidence interval.

parameters.name: comparison_2024_value

provenance.detail: Inverse-distance weighted 2024 value from 20 comparison counties

parameters.transformation: Subtracted from host and used as denominator

estimates.confidence_rationale: The benchmark is reproducible but the short post-opening window and concurrent county treatments prevent attribution.
estimates.decision_relevance: Shows the county's 2024 divergence from a transparent comparison benchmark without assigning the difference to Expedient.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: A causal design with complete county exposure history, treatment isolation, pre-trends, placebos, spillover rules and robustness checks

assumptions: Matching uses 2013-2020 log level, average log growth, and growth volatility.
Study counties are excluded from the donor pool.
The 2021 opening is not assumed to be first county exposure or an isolated treatment date.

limitations: This comparison is descriptive and must not be interpreted as a data-center effect.
Milwaukee County contains other data centers and concurrent investments.
The donor screen cannot exclude every unobserved treatment.
The interval is fit sensitivity, not statistical confidence.
estimates.notes: Descriptive benchmark gap only; no causal_design metadata is attached.
